concerns.text: Tasks T001, T002 and T003 are all marked **[P]** (parallel‑safe) but T002 depends on the outcome of T001 (it runs only if all real fetches fail) and T003 depends on the results of T001/T002. This hidden ordering makes the [P] tag unsafe.
Tasks T022 and T023 are marked **[P]** yet they consume every artifact produced by the entire pipeline. They cannot be run in parallel with upstream tasks; the [P] tag is therefore incorrect.

Task T007 expects a raw source (real or simulated) to read and standardize, but no preceding task creates the file `data/raw/standardized.csv` (or places the fetched/simulated data there). The producer of the raw standardized dataset is missing, causing a consumer‑before‑producer ordering violation.

User Story 2 (tasks T014‑T016) is not independently shippable: it requires the train/test splits produced by User Story 1 (T013). Each US block should be testable end‑to‑end on its own; US2 therefore violates the independent‑shippable‑unit rule.
User Story 3 (tasks T017‑T021) depends on models trained in User Story 2 and on data splits from User Story 1, so it is not an independently shippable unit either.

Duplicate task identifiers are not present in the current list, but the earlier analysis flagged a potential duplication (e.g., T009, T010, T011) that does not exist. Ensure task IDs are unique to avoid traceability ambiguity.
